items.title: The Third Numeric Category Opens: The Ten Unwholesome Courses of Action, Analysed Four Ways

items.zh: 已說二種佛教所應知處。次說三種，謂依十相、三門、三種及與三根，於諸有情發起邪行，能令有情墮諸惡趣。言十相者，謂壞生命、財物、妻妾，若壞實義、善友、讚美所為事業，若意三濁。謂執受他財欲為己有，欲令他遭所不愛事，誹謗真實所有惡見。言三門者，一、作業毀壞門，二、意樂毀壞門，三、方便毀壞門。於十相中，前之七種作業毀壞；其次二種意樂毀壞；最後一種方便毀壞，所謂惡見。由惡見故，羞恥、慈悲、離諸惡行悉皆毀壞；無有羞恥、無有慈悲，廣造眾惡。言三種者，一、身所作，二、語所作，三、意所作。言三根者，一、為自饒益相，二、為損害他相，三、於他顛倒相。謂於非法而作法想、於不應作作應作想，堅執現行。
items.en: The Ground of What Is Attained Through Hearing, the tenth, part two, in the Basic Section. The two-thing category of what a Buddhist should know has now been explained. Next, the three-thing category. By way of ten marks, three gateways, three kinds, and three roots, one gives rise to wrongdoing towards sentient beings that causes them to fall into the evil destinies. The ten marks: destroying life, property, or another's spouse; destroying truth, good friendship, or praiseworthy conduct; and the mind's three defilements. Namely: seizing another's wealth, wishing to make it one's own; wishing to bring about what another does not desire; and the wrong view that slanders what is genuinely real. The three gateways: first, the gateway of ruinous action; second, the gateway of ruinous intention; third, the gateway of ruinous means. Among the ten marks, the first seven are ruinous action; the next two are ruinous intention; and the last, wrong view, is ruinous means. Because of wrong view, shame, compassion, and the capacity to abandon unwholesome conduct are all destroyed; lacking shame and lacking compassion, one commits evil extensively. The three kinds: first, what is done by the body; second, what is done by speech; third, what is done by the mind. The three roots: first, the mark of benefiting oneself; second, the mark of harming another; third, the mark of inverted [understanding] towards another. Namely: taking what is not the Dharma to be the Dharma, taking what should not be done to be what should be done, and firmly clinging to and carrying it out.

items.title: What Leaves the Senses Unguarded, and the Four Seeds Underlying Every Phenomenon

items.zh: 復有三法，能令有情不護諸根。一、於依止中邪法種子，二、於諸境界取不正相，三、於私隱處不正思惟。如是三種，當知即是欲貪、瞋恚及與害品。依四處所，發生三種不正尋思。謂於自己利等四種白品法處為欲獲得，或為不失，生欲尋思。於能障彼怨、中二品有情處所，生恚尋思。於親友品有情處所，生害尋思。所以者何？若親友品或時違犯，於彼不生全斷滅欲，唯有輕微苦楚方便訓罰之欲。與此相違所有白品，如應當知。略有四種內法種子，遍攝一切諸法種子。一、世間種子，二、出世種子，三、不清淨種子，四、清淨種子。世間種子者，謂欲、色、無色界繫諸行種子。出世種子者，謂能證三乘及三乘果八聖道等清淨種子。不清淨種子者，謂欲界繫諸行種子。清淨種子復有二種。一、世間淨，二、出世間淨。色無色繫諸行種子，名世間淨；能證三乘及三乘果八聖道等所有種子，名出世淨。
items.en: There are also three phenomena that cause a being not to guard the sense-faculties: first, the wrong-dharma seeds within one's own support; second, taking a wrong mark with respect to sense-objects; third, unwholesome reflection in private. These three should be known as desire-craving, hostility, and the class of harmful intent. Namely: with respect to the four bright objects — benefit and the rest — belonging to oneself, wishing to attain them or not to lose them, one gives rise to a thought of desire. Towards beings of the hostile or neutral class who obstruct these, one gives rise to a thought of hostility. Towards beings of the friendly class, one gives rise to a thought of harm. The reverse of this is the corresponding bright side, to be understood accordingly. There are, briefly, four inner-dharma seeds that comprehend the seeds of all phenomena: first, worldly seeds; second, supramundane seeds; third, impure seeds; fourth, pure seeds. Worldly seeds are the seeds of formations bound to the desire, form, and formless realms. Supramundane seeds are the pure seeds capable of realising the three vehicles and their fruits, the noble eightfold path and the rest. Impure seeds are the seeds of formations bound to the desire realm. Pure seeds are, further, of two kinds: worldly purity and supramundane purity. The seeds of formations bound to the form and formless realms are called worldly purity; the seeds capable of realising the three vehicles and their fruits, the noble eightfold path and the rest, are called supramundane purity.

items.title: The Three Cravings and the Three Seekings, Named Three Ways

items.zh: 復有三種從因所生有漏法因，若於此中不如正理修方便者，能生諸苦；若能如理修方便者，於苦於因、能知能斷。謂於欲界繫法染污希求，於色無色界繫法亦爾。又有三種諸煩惱趣，令諸有情流轉生死。謂於勝欲發意悕求，名初煩惱趣。於色無色界勝自體中發意悕求，名第二煩惱趣。於邪解脫發意悕求，名第三煩惱趣。又有三種諸有情類欲為根本作業方便。一、為得勝欲，二、為得勝自體，三、為證勝解脫道。
items.en: There are also three causes of phenomena with outflow arising from a cause: if one does not cultivate the means correctly with respect to these, suffering results; if one cultivates the means correctly, one is able to know the suffering and able to sever its cause. Namely: defiled craving for phenomena bound to the desire realm, and likewise for phenomena bound to the form and formless realms. There are also three courses of affliction that cause sentient beings to wander through birth and death. Giving rise to the intention to seek superior desires is the first course of affliction. Giving rise to the intention to seek a superior existence within the form or formless realm is the second course of affliction. Giving rise to the intention to seek a false liberation is the third course of affliction. There are also three kinds of sentient beings for whom desire is the root of their action and effort: first, [those acting] to attain superior desires; second, to attain a superior existence; third, to realise the supreme path of liberation.

items.title: Three Powers That Draw a Being Into Rebirth, and Three Kinds of Ignorance Across the Three Times

items.zh: 又有三種諸有情類於三界中攝受自體諸行威勢。一、牽引威勢，二、能得威勢，三、成滿威勢。牽引威勢者，謂能引之業。能得威勢者，謂健達縛正現在前。成滿威勢者，謂住於此受淨不淨諸業異熟。又有三種無明蘊。諸有情類住無明者，由此因緣，能生三世自體差別。謂於過去世前際等無知，能生現在自體；於現在世前際等無知，能生未來自體；於未來世前際等無知，即於未來能生後後當來自體。
items.en: There are also three powers by which sentient beings, within the three realms, take up the formations of their own existence: first, the power of drawing forth; second, the power of attaining; third, the power of bringing to completion. The power of drawing forth is the karma that draws one on. The power of attaining is the intermediate-state being actually present. The power of bringing to completion is dwelling within this existence, experiencing the ripened result of pure and impure karma. There are also three aggregates of ignorance. Sentient beings who dwell in ignorance, by this cause, generate the distinct existences of the three times. Namely: ignorance of the prior limit and the rest regarding the past generates the existence of the present; ignorance of the prior limit and the rest regarding the present generates the existence of the future; and ignorance of the prior limit and the rest regarding the future generates, within the future itself, existence after existence to come.

blocks.text: Fascicle 14 completes the fourth aspect of "inner wisdom" by arranging teachings by number, as the Āgamas do: things in threes, fours, fives, sixes, and sevens. It reads like a compressed Abhidharma dictionary. Many lists repeat earlier ones from a new angle; the commentary highlights what is new and what our teachers stress. Read briskly, and pause where a list speaks to your practice.

subs.head: The ten unwholesome courses, four ways

blocks.text: The ten unwholesome courses of action (Day 56) are analysed through gateways: the first seven are **ruinous action**, the next two (covetousness, ill will) **ruinous intention**, and the last, wrong view, **ruinous means**. Master Cháng Bǎi: wrong view is "ruinous means" because right view is the means to the noble path, and wrong view removes it.
"Taking what is not the Dharma to be the Dharma": Master Cháng Bǎi's examples are killing for sacrifice and fire-worship as a road to blessings (Day 47).

Three things leave the senses unguarded: wrong-dharma seeds in one's own support; taking a wrong mark of objects; and unwholesome reflection in private. The first is the root (seeds), the second the trigger (attention to attractive marks, Day 78), the third the habit that grows in secret. All three apply to each of desire, hostility, and harm, as the *Pīxún jì* notes.

subs.head: Three cravings, three destinies, three seekings

blocks.text: Craving for sense pleasure, for existence, and for non-existence. Three "destinies" of affliction; the third is seeking a false liberation. Master Cháng Bǎi: like non-Buddhists who take meditation for nirvāṇa (Day 51).

Three powers draw a being into existence: **drawing forth** (the karma that draws one on), **attaining** (the intermediate being present), and **completion** (experiencing the result). This compresses Days 5–6 and 65 into three words.

Ignorance of the prior limit, the later limit, and both: not knowing where one came from, where one is going, or how the present connects them. (Ru-Yi's English keeps only the first; the *Pīxún jì* reads all three.)

A reflection for the day: almost everything in today's lists can be watched in a single afternoon. The senses unguarded, an attractive mark taken up, a private daydream, a craving for more, and not knowing how this moment connects to the last: the treatise's numbered lists are maps of ordinary experience.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, which of the ten marks belong to the gateway of ruinous action?
options: the first seven; the next two are ruinous intention, and the last, wrong view, is ruinous means
quiz.why: "Among the ten marks, the first seven are ruinous action; the next two are ruinous intention; and the last, wrong view, is ruinous means." Master Cháng Bǎi, citing the *Pixunji*: the seven are deeds of body and speech; greed, hatred, and wrong view are the mind's three defilements.

quiz.q: Why is wrong view called the gateway of ruinous "means," per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: because wrong view is easiest to correct
because right view is the means to accomplish the noble path, and wrong view removes that means
because wrong view only harms others
because wrong view is bodily action
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Because right view is the means to accomplish the noble path, and wrong view removes this means, it is called the gateway of ruinous means." The treatise adds that through wrong view, shame and compassion are destroyed and one commits evil widely.

quiz.q: What example does Master Cháng Bǎi give of "taking what is not the Dharma to be the Dharma"?
options: non-Buddhists who think killing for sacrifice is meritorious, or fire-worshipers who think tending fire brings blessings
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: some non-Buddhists think killing for sacrifice is meritorious — unlawful, yet held lawful; or fire-worship thought to bring blessings: "taking non-Dharma as Dharma." This is the third root, inverted understanding. Venerable Miào Jìng adds mistaking an ordinary being for a saint.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, which three phenomena cause a being not to guard the sense-faculties?
options: wrong-dharma seeds within one's support, taking a wrong mark of objects, and unwholesome reflection in private
quiz.why: "First, the wrong-dharma seeds within one's own support; second, taking a wrong mark with respect to sense-objects; third, unwholesome reflection in private." Master Cháng Bǎi: the third is failing to be careful when alone.

quiz.q: The treatise speaks of "the four bright objects — benefit and the rest." Per Master Cháng Bǎi citing the Pixunji, what are they?
options: benefit, fame, praise, and pleasure among the eight worldly conditions
quiz.why: The *Pixunji*: among the eight worldly conditions, benefit, fame, praise, and pleasure are the four places; wishing to gain or not lose them gives rise to desire-thought. Venerable Miào Jìng: these are the "eight winds."

quiz.q: The third destiny of affliction is seeking a false liberation. What examples does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: non-Buddhists who take meditation for nirvāṇa — the five present-life nirvāṇa theories — or who hold that cow- and dog-vows lead to heaven
seeking rebirth in a pure land
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: false liberation is like non-Buddhists taking meditation for nirvāṇa — the five theories of present-life nirvāṇa — or holding that cow- and dog-vows lead to heaven. Venerable Miào Jìng: taking the absorptions for nirvāṇa is false liberation.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what are the three powers by which beings take up existence?
options: drawing forth is the karma that draws; attaining is the intermediate-state being present; completion is experiencing the ripening of karma
all three are the intermediate state
quiz.why: "The power of drawing forth is the karma that draws one on. The power of attaining is the intermediate-state being actually present. The power of bringing to completion is dwelling within this existence." The *Pixunji*: karmic existence, intermediate existence, and the existence of experiencing fruit.
